pages.title: Equipment Behavior and Balance Reference
pages.intro: GD-TOOL-01 preserves four distinct ways of delivering water. The following numbers are CURRENT values from FireEquipment.cs and FireRun.cs, provided for migration and comparison. They are not approved balance for manual refilling. Water quantities use game units; range and width use forest units; speed uses world metres per second.

blocks.text: Power is a configuration coefficient interpreted by delivery mode, not universal damage per second. CURRENT pistol pulses apply Power × 0.22 with 0.22 seconds cooldown. Cannon charge reaches full in 1.2 seconds; release uses Power × (0.6 + charge) and radius 1.2 + 2 × charge + 0.2 × upgrade in forest units, with 0.6 seconds cooldown. Cancellation never counts as release.

items: GD-TOOL-02 Foam: forgiving short sweep and wet protection. It teaches landing a stream, controlling duration and making a wet boundary. Keep its target response readable even when the tank empties mid-sweep.
GD-TOOL-03 Pistol: discrete accurate packets for isolated fires, exposed tower fill targets and gaps between scenery. Repeated fire must visibly preserve individual shot timing.

GD-TOOL-04 Fan: five streams for adjacent flames. Spread divides coverage; it must not receive five full-strength damage awards from one accounting step. Higher consumption makes efficient positioning valuable.

GD-TOOL-05 Cannon: an aimed arcing water bomb for dense groups. Show charge, expected landing and cost. Support the existing offhand pump and accessible pinch-charge alternative; never require both. Recoil moves the tool presentation slightly, never the camera or authoritative aim.

blocks.text: CURRENT tuning adds 25 capacity, 27 power, 2.5 range, 0.16 width and 0.2 speed per level, up to four levels. Preserve these values as a reference preset while measuring the new refill loop. PROPOSED upgrades change capacity without granting water. Near-empty cannon behavior must be explicit: cap charge to affordable cost and display the cap; below eight units show Refill and refuse charge.

GD-TOOL-06 acceptance records water consumed, hits, time to contain and refill duration per tool in the same cluster. Check charge cancellation, impacts after switching, fan overlap and partially filled tanks. A larger area must not silently increase reward count or let the visual splash apply a second hit.

pages.title: Salvage Modifications and Session Presentation
pages.intro: GD-MOD-01 gives discoveries a concrete use after the core water and reward loop is stable. These are PROPOSED M3 sidegrades, separate from the existing numerical tuning levels. Keep them optional so a missed crate cannot block the expedition.

blocks.text: STARTING TARGET: sector 2 and 3 each offer one optional Part; sector 4 and 5 offer two each. A blueprint found earlier unlocks its recipe early; the listed clear milestone also unlocks it deterministically. Duplicate blueprint claims convert to one Part exactly once. Parts remain pending until settlement. Crafting at camp consumes Parts once and creates permanent ownership for that expedition. Each tool has one mod slot; owned mods can be fitted or removed freely at camp, with no water or cash grant. Apply modifiers after base tuning; validate positive finite results.

GD-UI-01 keeps the fireground panel compact: sector name, remaining burning targets, tank amount/capacity and current task. The tool itself carries its water gauge and charge indicator. At low water, pulse the gauge once and point toward the available source; avoid repeated voice or flashing warnings. During SearchSafe replace combat instructions with finds remaining, animals available and a visible Next button. Next with outstanding finds shows a brief Leave or Keep Searching choice.

GD-UI-02 presents settlement as separate rows for eligible trees, clear bonus, cabins, coins found and animals rescued, followed by the committed total. One rescued animal grants a proposed 25 coins; author one in sector 3 and 4, and two in sector 5. No rescue is required. Camp shows owned tools, prices, unlock conditions, current and upgraded values, mod recipes and water still in each tank. Display empty new equipment before purchase; every sector retains a free supply.

GD-FEEL-01 targets 2 to 4 minutes of active suppression per later sector, followed by 30 to 90 seconds of voluntary search. These are hypotheses, not time limits. Start with a full 60-unit extinguisher only on New Expedition; all other transitions preserve or restore checkpoint amounts. Target refilling at 15 to 25 percent of active interaction time; tune power, capacity or source flow if players spend most of a session pumping. Search has no timer. Refill confirmation, water impact and accepted pickup should respond within the next presented frame after their domain event; measure actual latency on-device.
